stories.title: Connah’s Quay Salvation Army marks 135 years with weekend of celebrations
stories.summary: The Salvation Army’s leaders for the UK and Ireland are returning to Connah’s Quay this weekend, where they once led the town’s church, to mark its 135th anniversary. Commissioners Jenine and Paul Main led the Connah’s Quay church for four years between 1988 and 1992, and both of their children were born during that time.

stories.title: Liquidated manufacturer’s £67,000 rates debt to be written off by Flintshire council
stories.summary: lintshire County Council never had the chance to chase a £67,000 business rates debt before the firm that owed it went bust, a report reveals. Senior councillors will be asked on Tuesday 16 June to write off £67,250.41 owed by Westminster Worldwide Trading Ltd, a manufacturer based at Minerva House on Chester West Employment Park.

stories.title: Number of people in homeless accommodation in Flintshire up 27% in a year
stories.summary: The number of people living in homeless accommodation in Flintshire rose by 27% last year, a report to senior councillors reveals. stories.title: Deeside-based Iceland signs retail letter urging action on youth unemployment
stories.summary: The boss of Deeside-based Iceland is among more than 80 retail chief executives warning the Prime Minister that government policy is making it more expensive to hire young people. Tarsem Dhaliwal, group chief executive of Iceland Foods, which has its headquarters on Deeside Industrial Park, signed the letter sent to Sir Keir Starmer on Wednesday

stories.title: Ty Calon says vandalism to 3G pitch fencing has cost £2,000 in repairs
stories.summary: A community hub in Queensferry says repeated vandalism to its 3G pitch fencing has cost around £2,000 to repair.
